samples.summary: Paste-time merge propagation iterates a merge span (rs × cs) that comes from store-supplied (remote-collaborator) metadata without any bound, so a hostile span value freezes the tab
samples.evidence: `clearCellsUnderMerge` (sheet.ts:925) and the new `mergeCoveredSrefs` loop in `paste` (sheet.ts:2330) iterate `span.rs * span.cs` cells and `await this.store.get(...)` per covered cell. Spans reach `this.merges` from `store.getMerges()` (sheet.ts:498), which for the collaborative store is unvalidated document data (`packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:997` copies `{...span}` straight out of the Yorkie doc; `safeWorksheetRecordEntries` only guards duplicate-own-key errors, not value ranges). A peer with write access to the shared doc can write `merges: {"A1": {rs: 1e6, cs: 1e6}}`; the next copy/paste that intersects it makes paste run ~1e12 iterations with an awaited store read each — an unrecoverable client hang (availability DoS). Mitigating context, which is why confidence is low: `rebuildMergeCoverMap` (sheet.ts:775) already performs the same unbounded rs×cs walk at load time, so the class is pre-existing and not introduced by this diff; the diff only adds another trigger. No validation of `MergeSpan` magnitude exists anywhere I looked.

samples.summary: The internal-paste branch is selected purely by clipboard-text equality, and that branch now also mutates merge structure (creates/deletes merged blocks)
samples.evidence: `if (this.copyBuffer && text === this.copyBuffer.text)` (sheet.ts:2193) is the only discriminator for the trusted "internal paste" path, which after this change additionally re-creates merged blocks (`pastedMerges`, sheet.ts:2221-2231) and, on a cut, deletes source blocks (sheet.ts:2325-2335). The system clipboard is a cross-origin surface: a page the user visits can overwrite clipboard text on a user gesture, so clipboard text is attacker-influenceable input deciding whether structural merge mutation runs. Impact is limited to the user's own previously copied content and layout (no cross-document read/write, no secret exposure), and an attacker must guess the exact buffer text, so this is hardening only — worth an explicit note that clipboard text is untrusted input rather than an identity check.

samples.summary: No authorization regression found: every entry point to the modified paste path is still behind the read-only gate, and the HTML paste parser remains inert
samples.evidence: Traced all callers of the changed `Sheet.paste`: `Spreadsheet.paste` guards with `if (!this.sheet || this._readOnly) return` (view/spreadsheet.ts:690); `Worksheet.paste` is private and its single call site guards with `if (this.readOnly) return` (view/worksheet.ts:5097-5099); the frontend context-menu path goes through `Spreadsheet.paste` (sheet-view.tsx:758) and the document-level paste listener returns early on readOnly (sheet-view.tsx:609). The pivot guard (`if (this.pivotDefinition) return false`) is preserved. `html2grid` uses `DOMParser.parseFromString(html, 'text/html')` and only reads `textContent`/`el.style.*` (model/worksheet/grids.ts:164-231) — inert document, no script execution, and the added HTML-paste test does not widen that surface. No secrets, injection sinks, crypto, or network calls (`fetch`/`XMLHttpRequest` absent from packages/sheets/src) are touched. Recorded so the verifier knows this ground was covered.
searchedFor: grep innerHTML|DOMParser in packages/sheets/src; read grids.ts html2grid
